what_its_for: Prednicarbate is a medium-strength steroid cream or ointment used on the skin to reduce redness, itching, swelling, and irritation caused by skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, rashes, and other inflammatory skin problems.
how_to_take: Wash and gently dry the affected area of skin before applying. Apply a thin layer of the cream or ointment to the affected skin and gently rub it in. Wash your hands thoroughly before and after applying, unless you are treating your hands. Do not cover the treated area with bandages or wraps unless your doctor tells you to. Do not use this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or vagina.
dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area 1 to 2 times per day, or exactly as directed by your doctor. Use only the amount needed to cover the affected area. Do not use more than prescribed. Your doctor will tell you how long to use it — most treatments last 2 to 4 weeks. Do not use it longer than recommended without talking to your doctor.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the tube or container tightly closed. Do not freeze. Keep this medicine away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Throw away any unused medicine after your treatment is finished.
what_to_avoid: Do not apply to your face, underarms, or groin area unless your doctor specifically tells you to, as the skin in these areas absorbs more medicine. Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes or mouth. Do not use on broken, infected, or open skin wounds unless directed by your doctor. Avoid using makeup or other skin products on the treated area right after applying the medicine. Do not use large amounts on large areas of skin or for a long time without medical supervision.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you notice: your skin condition is getting worse or not improving after 2 weeks of treatment; signs of a skin infection such as increased redness, warmth, swelling, pus, or pain; unusual skin thinning, stretch marks, or easy bruising; acne-like breakouts or excessive hair growth at the treated area; any signs of allergic reaction such as severe rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; or if you notice unusual weight gain, swollen face, or increased thirst and urination, which could be signs of too much steroid being absorbed into your body.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in redness, itching, and irritation within a few days of starting treatment. Full improvement typically occurs within 1 to 2 weeks of regular use. If you do not see improvement after 2 weeks, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Children: Use with extra caution in children. Children absorb more of this medicine through the skin and are at greater risk for side effects. Do not use on a child's diaper area. Always follow your pediatrician's instructions carefully. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medicine. Use only if clearly needed and for the shortest time possible. If breastfeeding, do not apply to the breast or nipple area. Elderly: Older adults may have thinner, more sensitive skin and should use this medicine carefully as directed by their doctor.
